sources.entry: The C4 model for visualising software architecture

summary.title: The C4 model for visualising software architecture
summary.one_liner: The C4 model is a hierarchical, notation- and tool-independent approach to diagramming software architecture at the levels of system context, containers, components and code.
takeaways: C4 uses a hierarchy of abstractions: software systems, containers, components, and code.
It defines hierarchical diagrams: system context, containers, components, and code.
Supporting diagrams include system landscape, dynamic, and deployment diagrams.
The model is notation independent and tooling independent, so it can be applied with any tools.
summary.summary: The official site for the C4 model, written by its creator Simon Brown, presents it as an easy-to-learn, developer-friendly approach to software architecture diagramming. It lists a set of hierarchical abstractions (software systems, containers, components, code), hierarchical diagrams built on them (system context, containers, components, code), and supporting diagrams (system landscape, dynamic, deployment). The page states the model is notation and tooling independent and links to a recorded talk from Agile on the Beach 2019. The page is brief and does not go into detailed examples or instructions.
